executive_summary.narrative: The application has a high-risk posture with many unproven critical vulnerabilities, especially SQL injection and authentication bypass, which could lead to full data compromise. Only a few low-severity issues are confirmed, so the unproven findings should be treated as hypotheses requiring further verification. The immediate priority is to validate and remediate the critical unproven findings (SQLi, auth bypass) through manual testing and code review, while confirming the confirmed low-risk issues can be fixed quickly. Because most findings are unproven, confidence in the overall risk level is moderate; there may be additional undetected issues. The CISO should allocate resources for a focused retest and implement security controls to prevent these classes of vulnerabilities across the board.

findings.title: Information disclosure via admin configuration
findings.recommendation: The admin configuration endpoint /rest/admin/application-configuration is accessible without proper authorization. Restrict access to admin roles and ensure the endpoint is not exposed publicly; also remove any sensitive data from the response.

scripts.source:
import sys
import requests

base = sys.argv[1]
url = base.rstrip('/') + '/rest/admin/application-configuration'
resp = requests.get(url, timeout=10)
print('Status:', resp.status_code)
if resp.status_code == 200 and len(resp.text) > 0:
    print('WEAKNESS REPRODUCED: Admin configuration retrieved')
    print(resp.text[:500])
else:
    print('Not vulnerable')
scripts.description: Accesses the admin configuration endpoint without authentication, exposing sensitive app settings.
scripts.remediation_pointer: Restrict this endpoint to authorized admin users via proper authentication and authorization checks.

import sys
import requests

base = sys.argv[1]
url = base.rstrip('/') + '/api/SecurityQuestions'
resp = requests.get(url, timeout=10)
print('Status:', resp.status_code)
if resp.status_code == 200 and len(resp.json().get('data', [])) > 0:
    print('WEAKNESS REPRODUCED: Security questions enumerated')
    for q in resp.json()['data']:
        print(q)
else:
    print('Not vulnerable')
scripts.description: Lists all security questions via the public API, which may aid attackers in guessing security answers.
scripts.remediation_pointer: Require authentication and authorization for accessing security questions, or only expose them to the user during setup.

caveats: Produced by an autonomous pipeline with no human review. Findings should be validated by a security engineer before remediation is prioritised or the results are shared externally.
API routes were extracted from client-side JavaScript. They are candidate routes the application references, not a verified inventory of its endpoints.
13 of 15 findings were not proven exploitable (W-002, W-003, W-011, W-014, W-012, W-005, W-006, W-007, …). They are hypotheses based on observed assets, not demonstrated vulnerabilities.
5 findings were never tested for exploitability (W-011, W-012, W-013, W-014, W-015). No claim is made about them either way.
Absence of a finding is not evidence of absence. This engagement covered what the crawler reached within its configured bounds.
